problem.text: The change addresses retained file handles during conversion by adding a second collection-close boundary; conversion already closed the module's collection immediately after loading unquantized weights.

reasoning.text: SafetensorsCollection caches native handle lists by filename. close() closes populated entries and resets them to None while preserving tensor metadata, allowing later get_tensor calls to reopen files.

impact.text: The additional cleanup releases any handles present after tensor collection and module unloading. Its incremental benefit depends on handles having reopened since the existing post-load close; no measured reduction is established.

source_notes.text: Issue #33, “Error converting model,” includes a “Too many open files (errno=24)” traceback through compile_model and the safetensors loader, followed by a May 7 report of successful conversion and later discussion of a separate GLM sampling problem. Its relationship to this change is inferred from the shared loader and handle-pressure symptom, not an explicit reference to this commit.

Other matching discussions concern different failures: #8 reports an invalid reshape, #11 an incorrect bias datatype, #16 an invalid CUDA configuration, and PR #13 missing BOS-token handling. Their connection here is inferred only from conversion-path overlap, not evidence that this handle cleanup fixes those failures.

Issue #34, “torch._C._LinAlgError on last layer of quant,” reports Cholesky failure; #38, “Error converting nvidia/Llama-3_1-Nemotron-Ultra-253B-v1,” reports incompatible tensor dimensions during loading. Their inferred connection is the shared convert_model.py path; neither report establishes a handle-exhaustion failure addressed by this line.

limitations: No conversion or native-loader execution was performed. Handle counts, platform limits and performance effects remain unmeasured.
No concrete reopening path between the existing post-load close and the new close was established.
A scalar computation would not validate this resource-lifetime change; meaningful verification requires observing actual file handles during conversion.

chapters.title: Close cached input handles after each conversion slice

claims.text: main now calls config.stc.close() immediately after module.unload() inside the current_slice loop. Thus cleanup occurs per slice, including the single-slice case, before saving the module's accumulated q_tensors.

The close targets input-loader resources rather than the collected output dictionary. After saving, the existing code exposes q_tensors through set_new_tensors, reloads the module from memory, clears that override and advances calibration state. close() requires new_tensors to be None; the added call precedes this override.

Native stloader_open_file opens a FILE stream for each loader thread. stloader_close_file closes every stream in the supplied list and frees allocated host staging buffers. The Python collection then marks the filename's cached handles absent.

This favors prompt resource release over retaining handles for possible reuse. Later file-backed reads can reopen them, whereas an already-empty handle cache makes the added close perform no native closes. The insertion is normal-path cleanup, not a finally block or a change to quantization mathematics.

annotation.summary: Adds collection cleanup after each conversion slice is unloaded, releasing any cached input-file handles before output tensors are saved.
